sections.html:
A Sammamish owner can sell three ways: list with an agent, handle the sale personally, or accept an as-is cash offer. The cash route moves fastest since no lender has to approve the buyer, though the offer will account for the condition of the house and for the convenience of a quick close.

Values here are high. The median for owner-occupied housing in 2020 to 2024 is $1,407,300, and 82.6 percent of homes are occupied by their owners. Most sellers therefore hold a single-family house on a plateau lot, not a rental. Population fell 2.0 percent between the April 2020 base of 67,457 and 66,110 on July 1, 2025.

  • An agent makes sense for a house that shows well, if a few weeks of marketing is fine.
  • A cash buyer suits a relocation, an estate or deferred maintenance.
  • Selling alone is realistic only if you can prepare the disclosure form and closing papers.

Judge each bid on four points: price, closing day, who pays which closing costs, and repair credits.

These citywide numbers frame what buyers here expect.

With about nine in ten residents staying put, turnover is low, and the buyers who do show up are mostly families after space and schools. Bedroom count, yard size and school district tend to carry weight in pricing. Commute questions are common too: a Redmond worker thinks about SR 202, while someone headed to Seattle thinks about I-90 and the light rail connection at Mercer Island.

Three people per household on average suggests family sellers moving up or down. If the house is larger than the people in it now need, a cash sale can shorten the gap between the old home and the next one.

sections.h2: Which school district is your house in?
sections.html:
District lines split the city along Southeast 8th Street. North of it, students attend the Lake Washington School District, with Eastlake and Tesla STEM high schools and Inglewood and Renaissance middle schools. South of it is the Issaquah School District, with Issaquah and Skyline high schools and Beaver Lake, Pacific Cascade and Pine Lake middle schools. A small eastern area belongs to the Snoqualmie Valley School District. Buyers filter by district, so put yours in the listing.

The line runs through the middle of the city, so two neighbors a few blocks apart can sit in different districts. Look up your address instead of guessing from the street name. Buyers with children often start their search with the district and narrow from there, which makes a correct label in the listing worth the minute it takes.

Zoning can add value to a lot. The R-4 zone allows up to 4 dwelling units per acre, a maximum floor area ratio of 50 percent for single-family homes and 40 percent hardscape coverage. A detached accessory dwelling unit in R-4 needs setbacks of 15 feet in front and 5 feet on the sides and rear, with a 24-foot height limit.

Accessory units are broadly welcome. The city permits up to two on a lot with a detached single-family home, whether attached, detached or converted from an existing structure. A detached unit is capped at 1,000 square feet, and an attached unit can reach 50 percent of the house or 1,000 square feet, whichever is larger. No extra parking is needed when the property already has four or more spaces. If your lot has potential, mention these rules in the listing, and tell buyers to confirm current standards with the city.

Setbacks and height limits matter most when a buyer is picturing a backyard cottage. Confirm the current numbers with the city rather than quoting them from memory, and keep a copy of the answer.

A plateau lot with room for a second structure may appeal to a buyer with extended family or a rental plan. Ask whether the existing house leaves space for a unit that would meet the setbacks, then describe the possibility without promising approval.

sections.h2: Roof, drainage and the disclosure form
sections.html:
Winters are cool and wet, and snow is rare. Inspectors pay the most attention to the roof, gutters, drainage and crawl spaces, and the state disclosure form asks about roof leaks in the past five years, standing water and drainage problems. Fix what you can before you list, and answer the rest plainly.

The completed statement goes to the buyer within five business days after the contract is accepted. Inside it is a notice that restrictive covenants based on race or other protected classes are void and unenforceable under RCW 49.60.224, and the form asks about homeowners' association dues, special assessments, shared common areas and recorded covenants. If your home is in an HOA, order the documents early.

sections.h2: Excise tax and property tax at closing
sections.html:
Washington's real estate excise tax is usually the seller's bill, payable to the county treasurer by the sale date. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 are taxed at 1.1 percent on the first $551,000, then 1.28 percent up to $1,551,000, with steeper tiers beyond. The local rate is layered over that. Escrow or King County can tell you the local rate, and which tiers govern a closing before January 1.

Property tax follows the parcel, not the owner. When the county meets its deadlines, statements are mailed by March 15, and each one has to explain the senior exemption and deferral programs (RCW 84.56.020). Bills of $50 or more are split into April 30 and October 31 halves. Treasurers may set up payment agreements on current or past-due taxes, so ask King County Treasury about your balance before closing.

Plan on the closing agent dividing the current year between you and the buyer by the closing date. Ask for a statement early so the contract numbers match what the county shows.

sections.h2: Checklist and how a cash closing works
sections.html:
Put these in a folder before any contract is signed:

  • Your deed and a loan payoff statement.
  • HOA bylaws, dues and any pending special assessments.
  • Permit and final inspection records for additions or an accessory unit.
  • The newest King County property tax statement.

Cash closings follow a brief script. Accept the offer and escrow opens. Title is searched, your mortgage is cleared from the proceeds, and you sign the deed in front of a notary. The county receives the affidavit and tax, and funds go out once the deed is recorded. Because no appraisal or lender review is involved, the timetable depends on title work and your own plans.

If the house has an accessory unit, add its permit file and any lease to the folder. If an HOA governs the property, ask for its paperwork on day one, since associations can take time to respond.

faqs.q: How quickly can I sell a house in Sammamish, WA?
faqs.a: Cash buyers can close when title work wraps up, often on your chosen date. Listings run longer through showings, inspections and the buyer's loan. Whoever buys, request the closing date in writing.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Sammamish house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Repairs are optional, but the state disclosure form is still required unless the buyer waives it or an exemption applies. Expect an as-is buyer to price in the condition.

faqs.q: Does the school district matter when I sell in Sammamish?
faqs.a: Yes, buyers search by it. Southeast 8th Street divides the Lake Washington School District to the north from the Issaquah School District to the south, and a small eastern area is in Snoqualmie Valley. Check your address.

faqs.q: Can a buyer add an accessory dwelling unit to a Sammamish lot?
faqs.a: In many cases. The city allows up to two ADUs where a lot has a detached single-family home, and a detached unit tops out at 1,000 square feet. Setbacks and height limits vary by zone, so check with the city.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Sammamish home?
faqs.a: Bills of $50 or more are paid half by April 30 and half by October 31. King County Treasury collects, and the closing agent normally divides the year between buyer and seller.
